title: Assessing Metabolic Activity of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Using Isothermal Calorimetry
author: Beilharz, Kragh, et al.

steps.title: Prepare planktonic culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate 5 mL LB broth with a –80 °C P. aeruginosa freeze‑stock, shake at 180 rpm for 24 h at 37 °C; filter the overnight (ON) culture through a 10 µm syringe filter, measure OD600 and dilute with sterile LB to a final OD600 of 0.005.

steps.title: Prepare surface‑attached biofilm (SB)
steps.instruction: Filter the ON culture through a 10 µm syringe filter, adjust to OD600 0.005 in sterile LB, dispense 200 µL into each sterile calWell™ plastic insert, cover with parafilm, place inserts in a 48‑well plate and incubate 24 h at 37 °C with shaking at 120 rpm; after incubation gently remove supernatant, wash each insert with 200 µL sterile 0.9 % NaCl, transfer inserts into titanium vials of the calPlate™, and add 200 µL fresh LB containing 0.2 % L‑arabinose (final concentration).

substeps.instruction: 5. Filter the ON culture through a 10 µm syringe filter.
6. Measure OD and adjust to OD600 0.005 in sterile LB.
7. Fill each plastic insert with 200 µL of the adjusted culture.
8. Cover inserts with parafilm, position in a 48‑well plate and incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 120 rpm.
9. Remove planktonic biomass by discarding supernatant and wash gently with 200 µL sterile 0.9 % NaCl.
10. Place inserts into titanium vials of the calPlate™.
11. Add 200 µL fresh LB supplemented with 0.2 % L‑arabinose.

steps.title: Prepare alginate‑bead encapsulated cells (AB)
steps.instruction: Filter the ON culture through a 10 µm syringe filter, adjust to OD600 2, dilute 20‑fold in sterile 2 % (w/v) alginate to obtain OD600 0.1, extrude the alginate‑bacterial suspension through a 21‑gauge needle into 150 mL of sterile 0.25 M CaCl₂ stirred at 150 rpm (needle positioned ~3 cm below surface and ~1.5 cm from beaker edge) at a flow rate of 30 mL/h using a syringe pump; allow beads to harden for 1 h, discard CaCl₂, wash beads twice in 50 mL sterile 0.9 % NaCl, transfer 20 beads to 50 mL pre‑warmed LB in a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask and incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 100 rpm; rinse beads briefly (<1 min) in 50 mL sterile 0.9 % NaCl, place a single bead into a calWell™ insert, position inserts in titanium vials of the calPlate™, and add 190 µL fresh LB with 0.2 % L‑arabinose (total volume 200 µL). Handle inserts with sterile tweezers to avoid spilling.

substeps.instruction: 12. Filter the ON culture through a 10 µm syringe filter.
13. Measure OD and adjust to OD600 2.
14. Dilute 20× in sterile 2 % w/v alginate to reach OD600 0.1.
15. Place 150 mL sterile 0.25 M CaCl₂ in a 250 mL beaker on a magnetic stirrer.
16. Stir at 150 rpm; position a 21‑gauge needle ~3 cm below the surface and ~1.5 cm from the beaker edge.
17. Connect the needle to a 20 mL syringe containing the alginate‑bacterial mix via sterile silicone tubing (ID = 2 mm).
18. Mount syringe on a pump set to 30 mL/h.
19. Dispense droplets into the stirred CaCl₂ solution.
20. Harden beads for 1 h in the CaCl₂ solution.
21. Discard CaCl₂ and wash beads twice by swirling in 50 mL sterile 0.9 % NaCl.
22. Transfer 20 beads to 50 mL pre‑warmed LB in a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
23. Incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 100 rpm.
24. Rinse beads gently in 50 mL sterile 0.9 % NaCl (<1 min) to remove non‑embedded bacteria.
25. Place a single bead into a calWell™ plastic insert.
26. Position inserts into titanium vials of the calPlate™.
27. Add 190 µL fresh LB with 0.2 % L‑arabinose (total 200 µL).

steps.title: Run biocalorimetry measurement
steps.instruction: Insert the prepared calWell™ inserts (SB, AB, or planktonic cultures) into the titanium vials of the calPlate™, load the calPlate™ into the calScreener™ instrument, and record heat‑flow (μW) continuously for the desired period (typically ≥24 h for fast‑growing P. aeruginosa).

steps.title: Prepare and analyse data
steps.instruction: Export raw heat‑flow data to a CSV file with equal‑length columns, then run the provided pca.py script (which loads the matrix of experiments × time‑steps, performs PCA with scikit‑learn, transforms to the first two principal components, and plots a labeled scatter plot).

substeps.instruction: 1. Gather metabolic signal data into a matrix (experiments × timesteps).
2. Run PCA decomposition using sklearn.decomposition.PCA.
3. Transform data to the first two principal components.
4. Plot the transformed data as a labeled scatter plot.
